items.title: FlyWire citation and data guidelines
items.claim: FlyWire public release data (latest v783, October 2023 snapshot) is licensed CC BY-NC 4.0.

items.title: FlyWire Codex
items.claim: Dataset tiles give 139,255 neurons for FAFB v783, 166,700 for MaleCNS v1.0, 158,262 for BANC v888 and 23,665 for MANC v1.2.1.

items.title: Shiu et al. 2024, A Drosophila computational brain model reveals sensorimotor processing (Nature)
items.claim: 91% of 164 testable predictions matched experiments (84% without the optogenetic screen); 95% is agreement between model variants; shuffled weights activated MN9 in 1 of 100 runs; the model omits gap junctions, neuromodulation and internal state.

items.title: Drosophila_brain_model repository
items.claim: MIT-licensed Brian2 LIF model; defaults to FlyWire v630; v783 files included; last commit 2024-09-14.

items.title: Male CNS connectome (Janelia FlyEM)
items.claim: MaleCNS v1.0 released 2026-06-08; the dataset is licensed CC BY.

items.title: Google Research blog on the male fruit fly connectome
items.claim: Headline figures: over 166,000 neurons and 125 million synaptic connections.

items.title: Virtual Fly Brain: neuron counts
items.claim: Independent reconciliation of fly connectome neuron counts by dataset and version.

items.title: BANC project repository
items.claim: BANC data on Harvard Dataverse is CC BY 4.0; the README quotes about 188,000 neurons without stating the scope; no licence file for the code.

items.title: Janelia MANC connectome page
items.claim: MANC (male adult nerve cord) is licensed CC BY; about 23,000 neurons.

items.title: Janelia hemibrain page
items.claim: The hemibrain (about 25,000 neurons) is licensed CC BY.

items.title: Winding et al. 2023, The connectome of an insect brain (Science)
items.claim: The larval L1 brain connectome has 3,016 neurons; the article is CC BY 4.0 and no separate data licence was found.

items.title: Eon Systems: embodied brain emulation
items.claim: By Eon's own description, hand-picked neurons switch pre-trained controllers; no body code is released, so the embodied fly is graded U.

items.title: DOOMFLY repository
items.claim: Full MaleCNS v1.0 LIF model plays Doom through hand-chosen read-out neurons; the learning experiment was negative; grade B.

items.title: NeuroCraft Fly public repository
items.claim: The repository contains documents and videos only; code and mod are "coming soon"; grade U.

items.title: Beat Saber fly post
items.claim: Viral claim with no code, weights or method published; grade U.

items.title: DesktopFly repository
items.claim: A 668-neuron FlyWire circuit runs, but behaviour states come from an ordinary state machine and animation; grade B, borderline C.

items.title: FlyCraft repository
items.claim: Navigation decisions are computed in Python and injected into the read-out neurons, contradicting "no behaviour is scripted"; grade C.

items.title: FlyDrones browser demo
items.claim: The browser demo runs a synthetic 850-neuron network, not connectome data; grade C.

items.title: Bad Apple fly repository
items.claim: The image is produced mainly by forced stimulation of neurons under dark pixels; grade C.

items.title: Flyhard repository
items.claim: All about 25.7 million connection gains are trained; parallel parking 0/50.

items.title: drosophila-brain-mlx repository
items.claim: Degree-preserving shuffle: MN9 67.30 Hz with real wiring vs 0 Hz shuffled (author-measured).

items.title: What a fly connectome adds to a body
items.claim: Replayed brain output 0/30 and shuffled brains lose 69 and 100 points on turning tasks (author-measured).

items.title: Larva connectome vs shuffles
items.claim: CIFAR-10 43.04% real vs 42.95% shuffled, p = 0.51 (recomputed by us from the published files).

items.title: FlyBrain reservoir
items.claim: Memory capacity 2.2 with MaleCNS wiring vs 15.5 rewired (author-measured).

items.title: FLM repository
items.claim: Loss per token 1.3598 with fly wiring vs 1.3593 without the graph (author-measured).

items.title: The Fly's Hash Function
items.claim: MNIST precision@16: real 0.499 < degree-preserving 0.552 < random 0.621 (author-measured).

items.title: FlyGym (NeuroMechFly v2)
items.claim: FlyGym 2.1.0 (2026-06-24) is a breaking rewrite of the 1.x API; Python 3.12 to 3.14; Apache-2.0.

items.title: State of Brain Emulation Report 2025
items.claim: Field-level assessment of brain emulation; used as further reading for the "mouse or human next?" question.

items.title: Mineault: deconstructing viral fly sims
items.claim: Independent critique of viral fly simulations (read through a summary tool).

items.title: flybrain.info projects list
items.claim: Community list of fly brain projects used as a starting lead; every published entry was checked against its original source.

items.title: Fly Brain Hub
items.claim: Competing directory used as a lead only; its data is not copied.

items.title: Drosophila_brain_model issue #7
items.claim: One sugar GRN ID from the v630 notebooks changed in v783; the successor ID fixes the KeyError (reproduced and fixed in our run).

items.title: Drosophila_brain_model issue #10
items.claim: Upstream silence() zeroes only outgoing synapses, although the Readme says "to and from".

items.title: Zenodo record of the FlyWire v783 connectivity export
items.claim: Lists CC BY 4.0, which conflicts with the CC BY-NC 4.0 in the FlyWire guidelines (read through a summary tool); the stricter reading is followed.

items.title: FlyGym v2.0.0 release notes
items.claim: FlyGym 2.0 was a full rewrite that dropped Gymnasium compliance, so older tutorials break.

items.title: Brian2 installation documentation
items.claim: Without a C++ compiler Brian2 falls back to the slower numpy target; a compiler enables the Cython target.

items.title: Introducing FlyOCR - I trained a fly brain to read a PDF
items.claim: Original upload by Jerry Liu (@jerryjliu0) on X on 13 Sep 2026, 0:40 long. Shows: A rendered fly "reading" a PDF: glyphs become receptor activity in a frozen MaleCNS circuit and a trained decoder outputs characters. Does not show: A small trained decoder does the classification; a plain pixel classifier (99%) and a small CNN (100%) beat it (89%) on digits.

items.title: I’ve successfully run the full retained MaleCNS v1.0 fruit fly connectome, all 166,700 neurons…
items.claim: Original upload by evnsnclr (@evnsnclr) on X on 4 Sep 2026, 0:09 long. Shows: A fly in a Minecraft box moving about while a panel shows modelled neural activity; claimed to run all 166,700 MaleCNS neurons. Does not show: Per its own README, hand-chosen readouts select scripted body programs and the body moves with inputs off; simulation code is not released.

items.title: did something similar, with a map of the brain showing which neurons are firing in realtime and…
items.claim: Original upload by Blendi (@BlendiByl) on X on 6 Sep 2026, 0:13 long. Shows: Minecraft fly with a live map of firing neurons and an on-screen readout of the chosen action. Does not show: A reflex layer is on by default and acts when the brain is quiet; looming and odour inputs are computed from game objects.

items.title: I'm training a fly brain to play Doom using the full MaleCNS v1.0 fruit fly connectome.
items.claim: Original upload by Alex Wormuth (@wormuth) on X on 6 Sep 2026, 0:07 long. Shows: Seven-second first-person Doom clip with telemetry panels, announcing that game frames drive the MaleCNS model's sensory neurons and damage stimulates two dopamine cells. Does not show: The "learning" did not work by the author's own logs; read-out cells were chosen because they responded to the screen.

items.title: Bad Apple but it's playing on a fly's brain
items.claim: Original upload by Kevin (@linguinelabs) on X on 6 Sep 2026, 0:38 long. Shows: The "Bad Apple!!" animation appearing as a pattern of firing neurons in the fly model. Does not show: The image is mostly the stimulus: neurons under dark pixels are forced to fire. The README says it is not a real brain simulation.

items.title: playing mario 64 using a fly's brain
items.claim: Original upload by Jessica Paquette (@barrelshifter) on X on 7 Sep 2026, 1:20 long. Shows: Super Mario 64 controlled from fly-model neuron activity: Mario runs, jumps and bumps into walls. Does not show: Hand-chosen stick and button neurons with smoothing, deadzone and jump cooldown; no goal or benchmark.

items.title: the fly brain can play beat saber
items.claim: Original upload by lyra bubbles (@_lyraaaa_) on X on 9 Sep 2026, 0:31 long. Shows: A fly-brain visualisation next to Beat Saber gameplay, with the fly apparently hitting blocks in time. Does not show: No code or method published; the author's replies reportedly say the motor output was fitted to a replay of the song.

items.title: the fly brain can play doom
items.claim: Original upload by Alex Wormuth (@wormuth) on X on 9 Sep 2026, 0:10 long. Shows: Ten-second clip of a rendered fly with a gun moving through a Doom level in third-person view, driven by the model's read-out neurons. Does not show: Hand-made frame-to-photoreceptor adapter and hand-picked output neurons; no shuffled-wiring control.

items.title: I gave the fly brain $100 to trade bitcoin.
items.claim: Original upload by Alex Wormuth (@wormuth) on X on 10 Sep 2026, 0:10 long. Shows: Ten-second clip of the fly model trading bitcoin, with dopamine neurons stimulated on profit. Does not show: README: profitable learning has not been demonstrated; paper trading by default; a hand-made decoder and risk limits sit between neurons and orders.

items.title: the fly has completed* the ultimate test: parallel parking
items.claim: Original upload by Breg Grockman (@alright_mark) on X on 10 Sep 2026, 0:25 long. Shows: A car in a driving sim attempting to parallel park under the fly-derived controller (the caption's asterisk hints it does not fully succeed). Does not show: All ~25.7 M edge gains were trained by behaviour cloning; repo reports 0/50 successful parallel parks.

items.title: A question going through all 165,122 neurons
items.claim: Original upload by IG Digital Lab on the project site, 0:24 long. Shows: 24-second visualisation of a question propagating through the MaleCNS model at fly.igdigi.com. Does not show: Controls have been run but not yet scored; so far real-brain answers look like the no-brain baseline (~0.50).

items.title: The First Multi-Behavior Brain Upload
items.claim: Original upload by Dr. Alex Wissner-Gross (@alexwg) on X on 7 Mar 2026, 0:43 long. Shows: Split screen: a simulated fly body walks in a sandbox, grooms and feeds, next to a point-cloud "brain" view labelled as a simultaneous brain emulation. Does not show: Does not show how behaviour is produced: by Eon's own write-up, a few hand-picked neurons switch pre-trained, imitation-learned motor controllers; body code is not public. Nothing is "uploaded".

items.title: How the Eon Team Produced a Virtual Embodied Fly
items.claim: Original upload by Eon Systems PBC on the project site, 0:40 long. Shows: Eon's own demo clip of the embodied fly (walking, grooming, feeding) that accompanies its technical explanation. Does not show: Same limits as the X version; read together with the page text, which calls vision "somewhat decorative" and the controllers pre-trained.

items.title: Dr. Philip Shiu - A computational model of the Drosophila brain (Brain Emulation Challenge workshop)
items.claim: Original upload by Carboncopies Foundation on YouTube on 11 Mar 2026, 1:20:57 long. Shows: Recorded workshop talk and Q&A in which Shiu walks through the leaky integrate-and-fire whole-brain model and its feeding and grooming predictions. Does not show: Long lecture (81 min), not a demo clip. Recorded February 2025, uploaded March 2026.

items.title: Srini Turaga - How to simulate a connectome? - IPAM at UCLA
items.claim: Original upload by Institute for Pure & Applied Mathematics (IPAM) on YouTube on 14 Feb 2024, 51:42 long. Shows: Lecture on simulating a connectome, covering the connectome-constrained model of the fly visual system that became flyvis. Does not show: Recorded February 2024, before the Nature paper; long lecture (52 min).

items.title: Artificial intelligence brings a virtual fly to life
items.claim: Original upload by HHMI's Janelia Research Campus on YouTube on 15 Mar 2024, 2:43 long. Shows: Janelia's overview of the virtual fruit fly built with Google DeepMind: an anatomically detailed body in MuJoCo walking and flying under a trained neural-network controller. Does not show: Body plus reinforcement-learned controller; no connectome drives it.

items.title: Anatomically accurate fruit fly body model
items.claim: Original upload by HHMI's Janelia Research Campus on YouTube on 15 Mar 2024, 0:17 long. Shows: Short clip of the anatomically accurate fly body model moving through its joints. Does not show: Kinematic demonstration of the body only.

items.title: We built an AI model to simulate how a fruit fly walks, flies and behaves – in partnership with…
items.claim: Original upload by Google DeepMind (@GoogleDeepMind) on X on 23 Apr 2025, 0:16 long. Shows: Square clip of the MuJoCo fly following a real fly's flight path, with the target path shown as dots. Does not show: Controller trained on recorded fly behaviour; not a connectome simulation.

items.title: A video of NeuroMechFly 2.0 in action
items.claim: Original upload by Pavan Ramdya (@ramdya) on X on 20 Sep 2023, 0:12 long. Shows: NeuroMechFly 2.0 walking toward an odour source, steering around a pillar with vision, and crossing rugged terrain with leg adhesion. Does not show: Per the post, vision is handled by a CNN and turning by an RL-trained network; not a connectome controller.

items.title: NeuroMechFly
items.claim: Original upload by BIOROB on YouTube on 23 Apr 2024, 0:40 long. Shows: How the NeuroMechFly body was built: a fly scanned by X-ray microtomography, segmented and turned into a simulated skeleton. Does not show: About the original (v1) body model; no brain model involved.

items.title: NeuroMechFly Workshop SFN 2024
items.claim: Original upload by Pavan Ramdya on YouTube on 18 Oct 2024, 57:23 long. Shows: Hands-on FlyGym workshop: installation, the control loop, kinematic replay and a vision-guided following example. Does not show: Uses the older FlyGym 1.x API (now flygym-gymnasium); code may not run on FlyGym 2.x.

items.title: FlyGym overview video
items.claim: Original upload by Neuroengineering Laboratory (Ramdya lab), EPFL on the project site, 0:40 long. Shows: 40-second overview montage of simulated flies in FlyGym environments. Does not show: Showcase montage; behaviours come from the controllers used in each example.

items.title: Fly Hemibrain Overview
items.claim: Original upload by Howard Hughes Medical Institute (HHMI) on YouTube on 22 Jan 2020, 1:46 long. Shows: Overview of the hemibrain connectome: about 25,000 neurons in the central brain and the circuits it covers. Does not show: Partial brain; superseded by FlyWire and MaleCNS for whole-brain work.

items.title: Janelia scientists and collaborators unveil fruit fly nerve cord connectome
items.claim: Original upload by HHMI's Janelia Research Campus on YouTube on 6 Jun 2023, 1:17 long. Shows: Announcement film for the male adult nerve cord connectome (about 23,000 neurons). Does not show: Nerve cord only.

items.title: The FlyWire Connectome
items.claim: Original upload by FlyWire Princeton on YouTube on 2 Oct 2024, 2:14 long. Shows: Official FlyWire release film: renders of the whole-brain wiring diagram and why it matters. Does not show: A map of wiring, not a simulation.

items.title: The first complete map of every neuron in an adult fly brain.
items.claim: Original upload by Cambridge University on YouTube on 2 Oct 2024, 0:45 long. Shows: 45-second announcement of the first complete neuron-level map of an adult fly brain (about 140,000 neurons, 50 million connections). Does not show: Wiring diagram only.

items.title: FlyWire Codex Tutorial: Search (2026)
items.claim: Original upload by FlyWire Princeton on YouTube on 23 Jun 2026, 6:01 long. Shows: Screen-recorded tutorial of the Codex search features, including AI-assisted queries. Does not show: Codex requires a Google sign-in.

items.title: Scientists Release "Wiring Diagram" Encompassing Entire Central Nervous System of an Adult Fruit Fly
items.claim: Original upload by Harvard Medical School on YouTube on 26 Sep 2025, 1:13 long. Shows: Announcement of the brain-and-nerve-cord wiring diagram of an adult (female) fly. Does not show: Wiring diagram only.

items.title: Male fruit fly CNS cell types
items.claim: Original upload by HHMI's Janelia Research Campus on YouTube on 6 Oct 2025, 0:31 long. Shows: One example cell of every neuron type in the male central nervous system (brain and nerve cord), shown in turn. Does not show: Wiring diagram only.

items.title: Example visual-motor pathway in the fruit fly
items.claim: Original upload by HHMI's Janelia Research Campus on YouTube on 6 Oct 2025, 0:51 long. Shows: Traces one pathway from photoreceptors to a descending motor neuron through the male CNS. Does not show: Anatomy of a real pathway; game demos wire their own, often different, input and output neurons.

items.title: Male Fly Brain Connectome
items.claim: Original upload by Howard Hughes Medical Institute (HHMI) on YouTube on 3 Sep 2026, 0:50 long. Shows: Render of the male fly brain connectome, framed around comparing male and female brains. Does not show: Wiring diagram only; this is the dataset every September 2026 game demo loads.

items.title: The History of Fruit Fly Connectomics at Janelia
items.claim: Original upload by Howard Hughes Medical Institute (HHMI) on YouTube on 3 Sep 2026, 6:43 long. Shows: Documentary on Janelia's fly-connectome effort from 2008 through the hemibrain to the complete male CNS. Does not show: History, not a demo.

items.title: How we built two new brain maps using Google AI
items.claim: Original upload by Google Research on YouTube on 3 Sep 2026, 2:24 long. Shows: Google Research Short on how AI-assisted reconstruction produced the male fly map and a companion brain map. Does not show: Methods story; no simulation.

items.title: I Put A Fly's Conscious Brain into Minecraft
items.claim: Original upload by Ro0oney on YouTube on 7 Sep 2026, 19:59 long. Shows: 20-minute build story of putting a fly connectome simulation into Minecraft, ending with in-game footage. Does not show: Title claims consciousness; our is-it-real review found no study measuring or supporting that.

items.title: I Put a Fly’s Brain in Minecraft. It Learned to Farm.
items.claim: Original video by SWOT on YouTube; now linked to catalogue entry FlyBridge (grade C): a trained 1,536-neuron FlyWire v783 subset inside a policy network, with scripted walking, aiming and clicking.

items.title: Scientist Just Uploaded Fly Brain to Computer
items.claim: Repost by Dr Ben Miles on YouTube on 12 Mar 2026, 1:16 long. Shows: Presenter explains the Eon embodied-fly demo in about a minute, framed as a fly brain "uploaded" to a computer. Does not show: Title says "uploaded fly brain"; our verdict is that no upload happened and the mechanism is not inspectable (grade U).

items.title: Researchers at Eon Systems have created a virtual fruit fly controlled by a simulated brain…
items.claim: Repost by Rowan Cheung (@rowancheung) on TikTok on 11 Mar 2026, 1:30 long. Shows: Vertical re-edit of Eon's embodied-fly footage with voice-over; the caption lists the model's limitations (simplified neurons, few behaviours). Does not show: Second-hand; the caption is more careful than the headline framing but still says the fly is "controlled by a simulated brain" without mentioning the pre-trained controllers.

items.title: Researchers have reconstructed the complete wiring diagram, or connectome, of the fruit #fly’s…
items.claim: Repost by Science Magazine (@sciencemagazine) on TikTok on 30 Jan 2025, 0:42 long. Shows: Vertical explainer comparing the fly connectome to a city map, using FlyWire renders. Does not show: Wiring diagram only.

items.title: The Internet Is Torturing a Fruit Fly... (opensource brain)
items.claim: Commentary video by Better Stack on YouTube on 12 Sep 2026, 6:25 long. Shows: Six-minute explainer of the MaleCNS release and the wave of Minecraft, Beat Saber, Doom and trading demos. Does not show: Commentary; check each project's own grade.

items.title: Software engineers have made a fruit fly play Doom, Mario 64, and Beatsaber
items.claim: Commentary video by PC Gamer on YouTube on 11 Sep 2026, 0:58 long. Shows: Games-press summary of fly-brain demos playing Doom, Mario 64 and Beat Saber. Does not show: News framing; does not show how inputs and outputs were wired.

items.title: Google AI roundup thread of fly brain demos (X)
items.claim: Google AI's own thread quoting the September 2026 fly brain demos; used as an index, it led to the original DOOMFLY clip.

items.title: doom-fly-control repository (commit 6b22922)
items.claim: Third-party controls with DOOMFLY's own code: real wiring 53.3 s survival, brainless constant autopilot 51.9 s, blind 10.5 s, shuffled 6.7 s, no connections 5.5 s; doomfly-rl scores the same with real, shuffled or no wiring; autopilot constants taken from the real fly's average output (author-measured, not reproduced by us).

items.title: doomfly-rl repository
items.claim: Trained encoder, fly-wired network and policy play Doom; shuffled and no-connectome controls score within one standard deviation (docs/controls.md; author-measured).

items.title: Fly Self Driving repository
items.claim: Trained MaleCNS rate network steers a car: 20/19/19 of 20 vs 16/20 rewired on the traffic task; headline numbers only in docs/results.md; one training seed (author-measured).

items.title: flydoom (mutkuoz) repository
items.claim: Untrained FlyWire v783 whole-brain Doom player beats a command-matched random agent only narrowly; mirrored eyes remove the advantage; no licence file (author-measured).

items.title: flyconnectome-nulls repository
items.claim: Standard random-wiring nulls out-evolve a compressed FlyWire v783 brain (1.78 and 1.77 vs 1.57); boundary-preserving nulls tie (author-measured).

items.title: Fly.exe repository
items.claim: Full MaleCNS v1.0 LIF simulation drives twelve FlyGym bodies through hand-picked descending neurons; only control removes the stimulus (12/12 vs 0/12); GPL-2.0.

items.title: FlyBridge repository
items.claim: A trained 1,536-neuron FlyWire v783 smell-pathway subset inside a policy network; scripted walking, aiming and clicking; no stored shuffled-wiring comparison; grade C.

items.title: fly-api repository
items.claim: Wraps the Shiu model for sugar to MN9; walking and visual demos use no connectome; navigation uses an 8,991-neuron subnet with a hand-set gain; grade C.

items.title: fly-brain (erojas) repository
items.claim: Full FlyWire v783 PyTorch LIF model steers a NeuroMechFly body, but grooming, flight, feeding and escape are scripted routines started at thresholds; grade C (borderline).

items.title: Haltere repository
items.claim: 30,000-neuron MaleCNS subgraph trained by imitation to fly an FPV drone; hand-written visual pilot sets the goal; 0/2 races vs 1/2 for a PD controller (author-measured).

items.title: Kick the Fly repository
items.claim: Live 166,700-neuron MaleCNS simulation triggers scripted game-physics reactions; circuit checks against matched control neurons with published failures; grade C (borderline).

items.title: FlyBrain-HalfLife repository (commit 0ba5548)
items.claim: Default network is generated from region sizes, not loaded from MaleCNS v1.0; real data only if the user supplies an npz file; steering and attacks computed outside the network; grade D.

items.title: FlyBrain Robot Bridge repository
items.claim: Only working brain backend is eight hand-set units driven by optical flow; the MaleCNS backend is an empty stub; grade D.

items.title: FlyWire neuron annotations repository
items.claim: Annotation tables for FlyWire v783 (release v3.1.0), accompanying Schlegel et al. 2024; no licence file.

items.title: Virtual Fly Brain
items.claim: Online atlas and query hub for fly neuroanatomy and connectomes, with Python and R clients and its own hosted MCP server (not tested by us).

items.title: I Put a Real Fruit Fly Brain Into Half-Life...
items.claim: Original video by Yusuf Temel on YouTube on 12 Sep 2026, 6:26 long, 137,648 views on 28 Sep 2026. Claims the MaleCNS v1.0 connectome; the released code does not load it by default (catalogue grade D).

items.title: Is the fly brain actually playing DOOM? (video file)
items.claim: Project-hosted video of the Doom control experiments (12 MB), linked from the README; link only, not re-hosted.

items.title: Fly.exe swarm showcase (video file)
items.claim: Project-hosted 1:38 video of twelve embodied flies on the MaleCNS connectome, linked from the README; link only.

items.title: flydoom 30-second clip (video file)
items.claim: Project-hosted clip of the FlyWire whole-brain simulation playing Doom, linked from the README; link only.
